beats.idea: The top of the file is a parts list: the app is a hub that pulls in concurrency, templating, signing, database, view and plugin pieces.
beats.shows: The learner can group the import lines into families and say what each family is for.

beats.idea: Async and thread imports show two worlds: asyncio runs the request, while a thread pool runs blocking SQLite work.
beats.shows: The learner can point at the asyncio, threading and futures imports and at the default of 3 SQL threads.

beats.idea: The template imports show that HTML pages come from templates that plugins and users can layer over the defaults.
beats.shows: The learner can name the loaders imported and guess why a choice loader exists: search order across template folders.

beats.idea: Signing comes from a third-party serializer library plus the secrets module; these back signed values and API tokens.
beats.shows: The learner can find those imports and the setting that allows signed tokens, which defaults to on.

beats.idea: The view and plugin-manager imports show the app owns the routing targets: each view class is a page or endpoint, and the plugin manager dispatches hooks.
beats.shows: The learner can list a few imported views (index, row, table) and the plugin manager import.

beats.idea: The settings table of named tuples is the first shared configuration defined in the module.
beats.shows: The learner can read the tuple shape and a few entries, such as page size 100 and query time limit 1000 ms.

brief.to: Next, we look at how the app turns these settings into configuration, databases and shared state.
